findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher compares the wrong substring and the condition is inverted
findings.body: The token id format is `<st:2><tt:2><gt:2>:<uuid>`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6 (`substring(4, 6)`). The matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant. It also returns false when the values are equal (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false`). For `onrtac` it compares `ta` with `ac`, never matches, and so never fails. The helper therefore only checks the `x:uuid` shape. Every `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` call passes `isAccessTokenId(<shortcut>)` and implies the grant is verified, but it is not. Wrong grant encodings would go undetected. Use `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The fourth `Objects.requireNonNull` is `requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. It re-checks `grantType` and never checks `rawTokenId`, so a null raw id is accepted. `encodeTokenId` would then silently produce `…:null` as the access token `jti`. Pass `rawTokenId` to the check.

findings.title: Grant shortcut length is never validated and the SPI Javadoc says 3 letters while the decoder requires exactly 2
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` is documented as "usually like 3-letters shortcut". The encoder just concatenates whatever the factory returns. The decoder (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`) requires the prefix to be exactly 6 chars and slices the grant at fixed offsets 4..6. A custom or future grant factory that follows the Javadoc and returns 3 characters, or returns 1 character or an empty string, produces tokens whose own id is later rejected with `IllegalArgumentException('Expected length of 6')`, or is mis-parsed. `postInit` only checks for duplicate shortcuts, not length or null. Validate that every shortcut is exactly 2 characters at startup, and fix the Javadoc to say so.

findings.title: Client credentials grant never records its grant type, so its tokens are encoded with "na"
findings.body: The PR registers a `cc` shortcut and the unit test uses `trltcc:…`. The grant type is only put into the ClientSessionContext in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, the password grant, the pre-authorized-code grant, the refresh path and standard token exchange. `ClientCredentialsGrantType` is not modified, and, as far as I recall, it builds its response via `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` rather than `createTokenResponse`. Its access tokens would therefore carry `na` as the grant type (`trrtna:…`). The same applies to the legacy token exchange, permission (UMA) and implicit/hybrid flows. The stated purpose of the encoding (grant-type-aware logic, e.g. #37117) does not work for these grants. Set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` in each flow that creates access tokens, or document that these grants are unknown.

findings.title: Session type is derived from the session at issuance time, so first offline-token issuance is tagged "online"
findings.body: The session type comes from `userSession.isOffline()` when the access token is built. For an initial login or direct grant with `offline_access`, the access token is created from the online user session. The offline session is only created afterwards, when the refresh token is generated. In the password grant the online session is even removed right after. The access token is therefore tagged `on…` although its session exists only as an offline session. The PR's stated goal is to look up only the session type the token came from (#37662), so such tokens would be looked up in the wrong store and fail. Take the requested `offline_access` scope into account, or otherwise derive the type from what the refresh token will use.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of a NullPointerException, not the intended validation
findings.body: The test only calls `factory.init(null)` and fills the grant maps by hand, so `sessionFactory` stays null. For `ofrtac:5678` the shortcut `ac` is not in the map, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut` takes its refresh branch and calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws NPE. The test catches `RuntimeException` and passes on that NPE instead of the intended `IllegalArgumentException('Unknown value … for grant type')`. The test does not verify the behaviour it claims to. Catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically and provide a mock session factory. There is also no test for `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` (session type, lightweight, grant attribute) and no integration test checking real issued token ids. `assertEquals` arguments are also reversed (actual first).

findings.title: New abstract SPI method and removed public constructor break existing custom grant implementations
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` is added with no default implementation. Every existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` stops compiling, and nothing is said about a migration path. The PR also deletes the public copy constructor `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)`, which is another source-incompatible change for any extension that used it. Provide a default (or make the shortcut optional) or call out the breaking change. In the same SPI change, add an upgrade note: the access token `jti` changes from a bare UUID to `<6 chars>:<uuid>`, which affects consumers that assume a UUID. No documentation or migration note is included.
